answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards. If several identities collude to fake independent demand, their deposits remain traceable to the same funding source and can be slashed when audits expose the pattern. The velvet, plume, and willow agents may look distinct, but creating more names does not multiply capital: the attacker must tie up funds per identity and risks losing them, making a Sybil swarm costly rather than free.
